findings.title: Loads, cart budgets and cable ratings are invisible in the world, so the load-budget lesson can only be found by trial and error
findings.problem: The whole room is built on numbers: oven 3, fridge 2, conveyor 1.5 (3 at start), lift 3 (9 at start), lamps 0.5 each, carts trip above 5, thin cable 3, thick cable 10 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:43,46-47,61). The player is never shown any of them. No appliance carries a load tag. The carts show only a bolt decal and an unlabelled gauge (src/props/prefabs.ts:163-168). The HUD dials have five unlabelled ticks (src/ui/lunch-hud.ts:10-16). The cables differ only by colour and bands, with nothing saying what they can carry. The only place the unit appears is the level tagline, 'five bars per cart' (src/levels/lunch.ts:15). The doc says the room's insight is 'everything together wants 10.5 bars … you can't run it all at once → prioritise and sequence' (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:25), but a player cannot add up what they cannot see. Every budget decision becomes plug in, watch the needle, maybe trip, retry. That breaks DR-31 (a player should be able to predict before testing) and DR-26 (the concept should be the mechanic; here the mechanic is guessing). It also leaves LR12 open: 'bars' are never tied to amps or watts. A player can still finish, because the needle eventually narrows the options, but the lesson they take away is 'try sockets until nothing trips', not 'loads on one supply add up against its limit'. This is the single biggest teaching gap in the room.
findings.fix:
Make the numbers physical objects without adding sentences:
(1) Load tags. Each appliance gets a chunky plaque of bar-pips: oven ■■■, fridge ■■, conveyor ■½ with a small spike glyph and 3 ghost pips, lift ■■■ with a spike glyph and 9 ghost pips, lamps ½. Build it with a new `loadTag(parent,steady,kick)` helper in src/render/kit.ts, called from buildKitchen, buildLift and buildLamps (src/lunch-runtime.ts:73-112) and on the fridge.
(2) Cart budget. A 5-slot pip strip on each cart, lit by the current draw (replace or sit under the gauge at src/lunch-runtime.ts:60 and :308). Paint a big 'A' and 'B' on the carts (prefabs.ts:166 decal) so the prompt 'cart B' matches the world.
(3) Cable ratings. Ring-band the plugs and reel: 3 bands on thin plugs, 10 on thick (or a ×3/×10 sticker on each plug, prefabs 'plug').
(4) State the unit once, on the cart plaque: '1 bar ≈ 1 A' (DR-32).
Keep the HUD dials, but put the pip scale on them too, so the world and the HUD read the same.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-teach-03/05/06 close-ups: each device shows its pips at zoom 9 and reads at the game camera. Blind test: a new player predicts 'oven + lamps = 4, too much for a thin cable' before plugging in. Add a unit test that every load id in lunch-runtime has a loadTag mesh.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches the claim. Loads are set only in src/lunch-runtime.ts:43 (oven 3, fridge 2, conveyor 1.5/3, lift 3/9, lamps 0.5), the cart limit of 5 is at :47, and cable ratings are at :61. No appliance mesh in buildKitchen, buildLift or buildLamps (:73-112) shows its load. The supply prefab (src/props/prefabs.ts:163-168) has only a bolt decal, a button and sockets. The HUD dial (src/ui/lunch-hud.ts:10-16) has five unlabelled ticks. Its red arc does start at 5/6 of the sweep, so the limit is marked relative to the scale, but no number is shown. Shot lunch-teach-03-carts-close.jpg shows unlettered yellow and orange carts with bare gauges. The only place the unit appears is the tagline at src/levels/lunch.ts:15. The fix is sound. A plaque painted on the cart is not a floating label, so it fits AGENTS 2.

findings.title: The capacitor's job (store charge, then supply the start-up surge) is never visible, so it becomes a key in a lock
findings.problem:
The capacitor cart is the room's headline idea. On screen, though, nothing shows what it does:
(a) It has no charge indicator. The green LED bar is a static lit material (src/props/prefabs.ts:172).
(b) At lift start it discharges 6 bar·s (charge 12 → 8.4 in my run, s5-solve log) with no visible change: no flash, no drain on the cart, no glow along the cap cord. Shots S-35 and S-36 look identical to S-33 at the cart.
(c) It starts full (charge:12, src/lunch-runtime.ts:44) although it sits unpowered in a dark storeroom. The comment at src/sim/electrical.ts:32-33 claims it 'holds no charge it was never given' (E-3).
(d) It recharges for free. src/sim/electrical.ts:35 and :41 add charge without adding any current to draw. In my run cart A read exactly 4.5 bars (rotate 135°) while the cap went from 8.4 back to 11.4 (E-2).
(e) The HUD needle with the cap docked goes straight to 4.5. The surge the cap is absorbing is never seen.
What the player actually experiences is: the lift trips → a badge with a schematic symbol over the blue cart → the marker points at the cart → 'Push the capacitor cart' → it docks by itself at 2 m → 'Plug into the capacitor cart' → it works. The concept being taught (stored energy supplies a brief peak so the supply only sees the steady draw) is entirely implicit. A player can finish by following the badge and prompts without forming any model of what happened (DR-26, DR-38). It also misses the most satisfying moment the room could have: watching the cart's charge dump into the winch as the lift lurches up.
findings.fix:
(1) Give the cap cart a charge gauge: each of its four blue cans fills with a lit band from cap.charge/12 (prefabs.ts:171 cans; drive them from LunchRuntime.render). Swap the static LED for a bar that pulses while charging.
(2) On discharge (cap.atLoad && kick active), play a bright pulse burst down capCord into the winch, step the cans down visibly, and make a 'whump'. Use g.burst at the winch and a Pulses instance on capCord (src/lunch-runtime.ts:56).
(3) Start the cap empty (charge:0 at :44) and make charging real: in electrical.ts, add `iCharge=min(1,(12-charge)/dt)` to draw for the source and every lead on the cap's route while it charges. The cart gauge then rises by 1 bar as the cans fill, and lift 3 + charging 1 = 4 < 5 still solves.
(4) Update the comment at electrical.ts:32-33 to match.
(5) Replace the schematic badge (lunch-runtime.ts:57-58) with the cart's own silhouette: blue cans plus a lightning drop. A novice cannot read the two-plate symbol.
findings.verify: New electrical.test.ts case: a docked, empty cap raises source draw by about 1 until full; at lift start, cap.charge drops by about 6 and source draw never exceeds the steady value. Retake S-35 and S-36: the cans visibly drop and the cord pulses. Retake a shot 3 s later: the cans refill and the cart A needle sits 1 bar higher during the refill.
findings.verify_reason: Checked with a node harness built from src/sim/electrical.ts (mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-teach/circuit-check.mjs). With the cap inline, the lift start never draws more than 3.00 on cart A. Charge falls 12 to 6.2 through the kick, then climbs to 9.2 over the next 3 s while the cart draw stays at 3.00. That is free recharge (electrical.ts:35,41). The cap starts at charge 12 (lunch-runtime.ts:44), which contradicts the comment at electrical.ts:32-33. The prefab LED is a static lit material (prefabs.ts:172). In shot S-36 nothing changes at the cart, and cart A's needle sits in the yellow at about 4.5. The badge glyph (lunch-runtime.ts:57-58) is the two-plate schematic symbol.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-teach/circuit-check.mjs output: 'cap: peak draw a 3.00 charge after kick 6.20'; '3s later charge 9.20 (from 6.20) max draw on a 3.00 -> free recharge'
findings.fix_correction: Step (3) as written breaks the intended solution. With conveyor running (1.5) + lift (3) + a charging draw of 1 right after the kick, cart A carries 5.5 and trips, because the recharge starts the moment the kick ends (electrical.ts:41). Keep the charging draw real but cap it so the clean route stays under 5: use about 0.4 bar (1.5+3+0.4=4.9). Alternatively, charge only while the lift is off, so the cap must be docked and charged before the lift starts, and then start the cap empty. Add the matching test: conveyor on, then lift with the cap, gives no trip during the recharge.

findings.title: A start-up kick is invisible: the trip happens in one tick, the needle jumps to full scale on zero current, and nothing happens at the motor
findings.problem:
The lift's 9-bar kick and the conveyor's 3-bar kick trip the cart on the first simulation tick (src/sim/electrical.ts:46). The player sees the HUD dial turn pink, and the needle is driven to full scale because the source is tripped: src/ui/lunch-hud.ts:49 (`g.tripped?180`) and the in-world gauge `gauge.set(source.tripped?1:…)` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:308). That is untruthful twice over. A tripped breaker carries zero current, so a needle at full scale tells the learner that a lot of current is flowing right now. And the actual peak, 9 bars, is beyond the dial's scale and is never shown.
At the motor itself nothing happens. Shots 21 and 22 at the winch show Pip, a slack cable and an unchanged winch. The spark and dust burst are 25 m away at cart A (src/lunch-runtime.ts:264), off screen. Nothing tells the player that the lift runs on 3 and only needs 9 for a moment, which is the entire reason a capacitor helps. A reasonable player who has seen the needle slam will conclude that the lift needs more than a cart can give. They will try the thick cable, which cannot help because the breaker is still 5, and get no new information. DR-28 requires the failure to show its cause at the faulty part. DR-47 requires each device to show its own state.
findings.fix:
(1) Add a peak-hold telltale needle (a red drag pointer) to both the HUD dial and the cart Gauge. It records the highest draw in the last 3 s, pinned past the red end with a '9' pip if it is over scale. The live needle drops to 0 on a trip. Store `peak` per source in Circuit.tick (electrical.ts:43-46) before the trip clears draw.
(2) At the motor that kicked: the winch drum jerks a quarter turn and stalls with a groan, the feed cable flashes thick and bright for 0.3 s (scale Pulses radius ×2 on that cable), and puffs come from the winch. Hook this on the 'trip' event when lift.started was within 1.5 s (the existing test at lunch-runtime.ts:269), and do the same for the conveyor.
(3) Show the HUD dial scale as 0–10 with the trip line at 5, so a 9 can be drawn.
findings.verify: Retake 21, 22 and 24. At the winch the drum jerk and cable flash are visible within 0.3 s. The HUD shows the red telltale at 9 and the live needle at 0. Add a lunch-hud test (DOM) that a tripped source renders needle 0° and a telltale > 150°.
findings.verify_reason: Harness result: with no cap, cart A trips on the first tick (event at t=0.0167). electrical.ts:46 trips instantly, lunch-hud.ts:49 sets the needle to 180 when tripped, and lunch-runtime.ts:308 sets gauge 1. Crop lunch-teach-24 shows the tripped dial A with its needle pinned past red, although no current flows. I reproduced the kick zoomed in at the winch (verify-lunch-teach-02-kick-winch-close-0.05s.jpg): the winch, drum and cable show no change, and the only cue is the HUD dial A turning pink. The trip burst plays at the cart (:264).

findings.title: The carts' 'breakers' trip instantly at 1.2–1.8× for one second, which real breakers never do. Reframe the carts truthfully as battery power stations with a surge rating
findings.problem:
src/sim/electrical.ts:46 trips a source on any draw above `limit+1e-6`, on the first tick. The kick trips are 9 on 5 (1.8×) for 1 s, and 6 on 5 (1.2×) for the conveyor after the lift. Under IEC 60898-1, a B-curve MCB must not trip within an hour at 1.13× In, must trip within an hour at 1.45× In, and trips instantly (<0.1 s) only at 3–5× In. So at 1.2–1.8× for one second a real breaker would not trip at all. The room therefore teaches two false rules of thumb: 'a breaker trips the moment you go a hair over', and 'motor inrush always trips breakers'. It also inverts the real relationship, because here the cable (src/sim/electrical.ts:49) is the slow, time-integrating element and the breaker is the instant one.
The prompt and HUD wording both say 'breaker' (src/lunch-runtime.ts:189, the bonus 'Never trip a breaker' at src/ui/objectives.ts:52). The room also never says AC or DC, and the capacitor-supplies-the-kick idea (L-1) is only true on a DC bus. On AC mains, a 'motor start capacitor' works by phase shift, not stored energy.
There is a truthful real-world device that behaves exactly as the game does: a portable battery power station. It has a continuous rating and a short surge rating, its electronic overload protection cuts out at once when a motor's start-up draw exceeds the surge limit, and buffering peaks with supercapacitors on a DC bus is real practice.
findings.fix:
Option A (recommended, keeps every puzzle number):
- Make the carts 'battery power carts': a 48 V DC decal plus a battery-cell glyph on prefabs.ts:166.
- Rename the protection in player copy to 'overload cut-out': lunch-runtime.ts:189 becomes 'Reset cart B's overload cut-out', objectives.ts:52 becomes 'Never overload a cart'.
- Call the capcart a 'supercap cart' in NAMES (objectives.ts:59) and in the prompts at lunch-runtime.ts:175 and :182.
- Add a comment at electrical.ts:46: '// electronic overload cut-out (like a battery power station's inverter), trips at once; tuning values'.
- Leave thermal-magnetic breaker curves for a later room that teaches them.
Option B: keep 'breaker', give Source an I²t accumulator (`acc+=max(0,(I/limit)^2-1)*dt`, trip at acc≥4) plus an instant trip at I>3·limit, and raise the lift kick to ≥16 so the lesson survives. That is more code and more tuning.
Either way, update the docs (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:9, GAME_DESIGN.md:23).
findings.verify: Grep player strings for 'breaker' in src/lunch-runtime.ts and src/ui/objectives.ts. With option B, a unit test: 1.5× for 0.5 s does not trip, 1.5× for 6 s does, 3.2× trips in the same tick. The tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts kick test still passes.
findings.verify_reason: The code facts are correct. electrical.ts:46 trips on any draw above limit+1e-6 on the same tick. Player copy says 'breaker' at lunch-runtime.ts:189 and objectives.ts:49 and :52. The room never says AC or DC. The real-world claims match standard IEC 60898 B-curve behaviour: no trip at 1.13×In, thermal trip within 1 h at 1.45×, magnetic instant trip at 3-5×In. A 1.8× peak for 1 s would therefore not trip a real MCB. AGENTS 10 names 'surges, capacitors' as taught concepts, so this goes beyond tuning. I did not open the cited URLs. Option A is a cheap copy-and-comment change and is the right recommendation.
extra_evidence: src/ui/objectives.ts:49 'Start the lift winch without tripping a breaker' (a third player string with 'breaker')

findings.title: Any intact cable lying across the puddle 'shorts' the supply, which teaches the folk version of water hazards
findings.problem:
LunchRuntime.wet() (src/lunch-runtime.ts:208) marks a whole cable wet if any segment passes within 1.2× radius of a puddle, and Circuit.tick (src/sim/electrical.ts:23) trips the source on a wet lead. In shot 16 the thick cable is laid through the leak with both plugs dry and far from the water, and cart B trips at once, with the warning badge placed at the puddle. In reality an undamaged insulated cord in water does not short. The danger is water at plugs and connections or through damaged insulation, which leaks current to earth and is what an RCD/GFCI detects. The game also calls it a 'short', which is the wrong mechanism.
This matters because the room otherwise works hard to be truthful. A learner leaves believing that a cable merely touching water is a short, so they cannot reason about why outdoor cords are fine but a plug in a puddle is not. It contradicts DR-33 directly and is listed as Known there; it is still open.
There is also a cheap way to keep the puzzle: the fridge socket (-4,-1.8) already sits next to the first puddle (-4.6,-1.2), and the doorway trail could be routed to cover a floor plug position.
findings.fix:
Change wet() so it tests exposed metal only:
- cable ends (both plugs, including a loose dropped plug);
- splitter ports;
- any cable flagged `nicked`. Set nicked when the door pinches it (lunch-runtime.ts:248, instead of an instant kill or as well as one) or when a bot drags it (:260).
Call the trip an 'earth-leakage trip' with its own water-drop glyph (see the fault-icon finding).
To keep the mop and bridge useful, extend PUDDLES so the leak covers the fridge's socket plate and the floor under the kitchen post's inlet. Then plugging in while the floor is wet trips, which is the real hazard: water at the connection.
Update docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:19 ('Cable in water = short').
findings.verify: Rewrite tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts 'a live cable through the leak shorts…': a thick cable routed through the leak with dry plugs keeps the oven on. A splitter or plug dropped in the puddle trips the cart. A door-nicked cable crossing water trips. Retake shot 16 under the new rule.
findings.verify_reason: wet() (lunch-runtime.ts:208) flags a cable when any segment is within r*1.2 of a puddle, and electrical.ts:23 trips the source on a wet lead. Shot lunch-teach-16 shows the thick cable through the puddle with plugs far from water, cart B's HUD dial pink, and the badge at the doorway puddle. RULES.md:217-220 lists DR-33 as Known with this exact cause. One overstatement: 'short' appears only in the internal event kind, the test name and the docs, not in any player-facing string. A grep of src/ui and lunch-runtime prompts finds none.

findings.title: The job card ticks off 'Power the feed post' and 'Mop up the leak' when a failing cable is merely plugged in, then tells the player to 'keep the oven on' while it is dead
findings.problem:
kitchenFed() (src/ui/objectives.ts:19) is true when any cable has 'kitchen' in its ports, is closed and is not dead. It does not check that the post has power. Step 2 ('Mop up the leak (or bridge it)', :43) and step 3 ('Power the kitchen's feed post', :44) are both done when kitchenFed is true, and steps latch forever (:100-103).
Two reproduced cases:
(1) A thin cable into the post. Step 3 ticks and the card moves to 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked'. Six seconds later the cable scorches, the oven goes off, and the card still says 'Keep the oven on…' (shot 13; log 'thin+6.3' shows oven:off).
(2) The thick cable through the un-mopped leak. Cart B shorts at the moment of plugging, yet steps 2 and 3 both tick (the leak step is skipped while the leak is the very cause). The card reads 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked' with water still at 1.0 (shots 16 and 17).
In the two most instructive failures of the room, the only text the player gets (AGENTS 2 allows just the card and prompt) congratulates them on the step that failed and points them past the cause. That directly undermines DR-28 (show the cause) and DR-42 (the card agrees with the world).
findings.fix:
Make kitchenFed mean 'powered': `g.lunch?.powered('oven')||g.lunch?.powered('kitchen-lamp')`, or route.source not tripped and lead not dead. Make step 2 done only on `water<.1 || (dry route: the feeding cable's lead.wet===false && powered)`.
Let the lunch steps un-latch while their condition is false and the next step's done() is false. Add an `unlatch?:boolean` field to Step and set it for steps 2 and 3, so that a scorch or short moves the dots back and the card shows the real current step again.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/lunch-teach/s2-fails.mjs scorch and short. After the scorch the card reads 'Power the kitchen's feed post'. After the short it reads 'Mop up the leak'. Add a tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts assertion that `.objective .cur` contains 'feed post' after the thin-cable scorch.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it (mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-teach/v1.mjs scorch). After a thin cable into the post, then 7 s, the oven is off and thin-1 is dead. The card shows three green dots and 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked', with the prompt 'Repair the burned cable (costs 15)' (verify-lunch-teach-01-scorch-card.jpg). The DOM text read right after advance() still showed the stale 0.9 s real-time flash text, so judge from the screenshot. In shot lunch-teach-16, cart B is shorted and water is still present, yet the mop and feed-post steps are both green. kitchenFed is objectives.ts:19 and the latch is :100-103.

findings.title: Second surge lesson (conveyor start on top of the running lift) has no cue at all, and the card's step order walks players into it
findings.problem:
The room requires the conveyor to start before the lift. The conveyor's 3-bar kick plus the running lift's 3 is 6, over cart A's 5 (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:38). The card orders step 6 'Start the lift winch without tripping a breaker' before step 7 'Send the tray up on the lift', whose marker then moves to the conveyor (src/ui/objectives.ts:49-50). In the trap run (s5-solve trap) I docked the cap, started the lift, and step 6 ticked done (liftRan latches, :49). Then I switched the conveyor on: cart A tripped at once.
What the player sees (shot T-37): only the HUD dial A turns pink. Nothing happens at the conveyor or the lift. No badge appears, because capHint fires only when the lift kicks with no cap (src/lunch-runtime.ts:269). The card reads 'Send the tray up on the lift' and still claims the breaker-free start was achieved.
After the reset, both motors restart together and the cart trips again. The plausible conclusion is 'the capacitor is broken or empty', which is the wrong lesson. Staggered motor starting is a real and valuable idea (vendor guidance for battery stations says to start one high-draw device at a time, because simultaneous surges overload the inverter), but here it is a hidden rule that can only be learned by failing blind, against DR-37.
findings.fix:
(1) Apply the kick-visibility fix (the telltale needle plus a jerk at the motor) to the conveyor too. The belt lurches and groans at the conveyor when its start-up trips the cart.
(2) Generalise capHint into a per-motor 'surge' badge: when a trip happens within 1.5 s of any load's start, float that motor's spike glyph over it (conveyor or lift), with no text.
(3) Make step 6 done only when the lift runs AND no trip happened in the next 3 s, or merge steps 6 and 7 into 'Send the tray up on the lift (without tripping a cart)'.
(4) Option: show the cart's pip strip as running load plus the hollow ghost pips of the next start, so the 1.5 + 3 versus 3 + 3 comparison can be read before switching.
findings.verify: Rerun s5-solve.mjs trap. The conveyor shows its jerk and badge within 0.3 s of the trip, and the card has not claimed the lift step. Add a tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts case: lift on with the cap, then conveyor on, expect trip:a and `snapshot().lunch.surgeHint==='conveyor'`.
findings.verify_reason: Harness: with the lift running on the cap, switching the conveyor on gives draw a=6 and an immediate trip. capHint (lunch-runtime.ts:269) requires !lift.capacitor.atLoad, so no hint fires when the cap is docked. liftRan latches step 6 (objectives.ts:49). Shot T-37 shows 6 green dots, 'Send the tray up on the lift', only the HUD dial A pink, and no cue at the conveyor or lift. After a reset, both motors are still enabled and the cart trips again (shot T-38).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-teach/circuit-check.mjs: 'conveyor after lift: draw a 6 tripped true'

findings.title: The fridge spoils the whole job at 120 s, yet the fridge is never a step on the card, and the intended solution never needs its 'time battery' idea
findings.problem:
The fridge warms at 0.006/s from 0.28 and fails the job at 1.0 (src/sim/lunch.ts:8-9), which is exactly t=120 s if it is not powered (s6 run: failed at 120.0). The 7 card steps (src/ui/objectives.ts:42-50) never mention it. It appears only as the third bonus star, whose text is hidden during play, and as the HUD thermometer. A first-time player who follows the card (wedge, mop, find out which cable feeds the post, possibly through a scorch, a short or a door cut) can easily pass 120 s and lose the job to an idea they were never introduced to. That is a fail state outside the taught concept's on-ramp (DR-02 'only a mistake in the taught concept', DR-37 'hidden rules shown before you can fail them').
Meanwhile the doc's fridge insight, 'the fridge is a time battery: unplug it while the oven bakes' (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:25,36), is never required. The scripted solution keeps the fridge on cart A for the whole bake (tests/lunch.spec.ts:19-20), and by the time the fridge is unplugged for the lift it is at 0.03 and irrelevant. So the room fails players for the fridge without ever teaching the fridge. On the positive side, the in-world cues before the spoil (sad icon, red thermometer, puff and groan, shot 42) are good, and the fail card is clear (shot 43).
findings.fix:
(1) Add a card step, or make the fridge a parallel 'keep alive' goal shown next to the chain, e.g. 'Keep the fridge cold' with the marker on the fridge whenever temperature > 0.55.
(2) Slow the first warm-up: start the temperature at 0.15, or warm at 0.004/s so the first spoil is at about 210 s, and keep 0.006/s once it has been powered once.
(3) Make the time-battery insight load-bearing. Put the conveyor's or lift's socket on the same cart as the fridge with a single outlet (cart capacity 1 at lunch-runtime.ts:50), so the fridge must come off for 20–30 s while it visibly warms but stays under 80%. Or retune so that kitchen (4) + fridge (2) is the only way to bake, forcing a mid-bake swap.
(4) Update LEVEL_02 to match whichever is chosen.
findings.verify: Blind playtest: five first-time players, count spoils before the first bake (target ≤1). Spec: tests/lunch.spec.ts intended solution includes one fridge unplug that raises temperature by ≥0.2 and still wins.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it with v1.mjs fridge. An idle room reaches temperature 1.000 at t=120.0 and fails (src/sim/lunch.ts:8-9: (1-0.28)/0.006=120 s). The card steps (objectives.ts:42-50) never mention the fridge. The spec keeps the fridge powered through the bake (tests/lunch.spec.ts:19-20) and unplugs it only for the lift at the end, so the 'time battery' from LEVEL_02:25,36 never matters. The cooler-box alternative (lunch-runtime.ts:230 sets cooled, which stops warming) exists, but it sits in the dark storeroom and is also not on the card.
extra_evidence: tests/lunch.spec.ts:32-34 (fridge feed moved to the lift only after the conveyor starts)

findings.title: Four different faults share one red lightning badge, and a door-cut cable is called 'burned'; the cause is never named
findings.verify: Retake shots 13, 16, 18 and T-37: four distinct glyphs, each at its cause. The toast text matches the cause and contains no fix verb. Add a unit test that each event kind maps to a distinct texture key.
findings.verify_reason: warningTexture (lunch-runtime.ts:14) is used by scar() (:212) for door cuts (:248), shorts (:264) and scorches (:265), and by the cart trip alert (:306). The prompt for any dead lead is 'Repair the burned cable' (:195), including a cable the door cut. Overstatement: the badge position (puddle, mid-cable, doorway) does carry some cause information. But at the cart, a surge trip and a sum-overload trip look identical (shots 22 and T-37), and the prompt mislabels door cuts. DR-28 (RULES.md:189) does allow one sentence naming the cause, so the toast idea fits the rules.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-lunch-teach-04-kick-survey-dark-store.jpg (same red bolt badge for a surge trip at cart A)
findings.fix_correction: Put the one-line cause sentence in the existing prompt pill, or the card's flash slot, for about 3 s rather than a new toast element. That keeps to AGENTS 2's 'card plus one-line prompt' text budget.

findings.title: Current pulses run at the same speed and density whatever the current, so the cable never shows that more load means more current
findings.problem:
Pulses.update (src/render/actors.ts:85) moves a fixed 3 slugs at `time*3/length`, the same for a 0.5-bar lamp, the 2-bar fridge and the 4-bar kitchen feed. LunchRuntime only switches them on or off (src/lunch-runtime.ts:320). In shot S-30b the thick cable's pulses are faint pale stripes that blend into its black and yellow bands, and the thin fridge feed shows none that I can read at the game camera.
The cable is the star (AGENTS 4) and the room's quantity is current through each cable against its rating. Making pulse rate proportional to current is the PhET-style way to make that visible, and it makes overload predictable: a thin cable visibly crowded with pulses is about to cook. Today heat is the only signal, and it arrives only once the damage has started.
findings.fix: Add an `amps` argument to Pulses.update. Speed = base·(0.4+0.6·amps/rating) and slug count visible = ceil(amps·2), with a pool of 12. Pass `this.circuit.draw.get(cable.id)` and cable.rating at lunch-runtime.ts:320. Use a saturated cyan with an ink outline so pulses read on the thick cable's bands. Keep the speed identical along a cable and on both sides of a load (DR-30).
findings.verify: Crop the kitchen feed (4 bars) next to the fridge feed (2 bars) at the game camera: about twice the pulse density. Over the thin rating, pulses crowd before the orange heat shows. A Pulses unit test covers count as a function of amps.
findings.verify_reason: Pulses.update (src/render/actors.ts:85) advances at time*3/length regardless of current. LunchRuntime builds 3 slugs per cable (lunch-runtime.ts:140) and passes only an on/off boolean (:320). In crop S-30b the thick cable shows two faint pale stripes that blend with its bands, and no pulses are visible on the thin cable. P1 holds because current per cable against its rating is the room's lesson and the cable is the star.

findings.title: Heat on a cable uses the same white→orange→red ramp as strain, and it cooks 33% over in 6 s on a linear (not I²) rule
findings.problem:
A cable lying on the floor over its rating turns orange (heat>.4) and then red (>1.2) (src/lunch-runtime.ts:318). That is the same palette the game teaches for strain on a held cable (AGENTS 4; the Playground). In shot 12 the slack thin cable glows orange-red exactly the way an over-stretched cable does, so a Playground graduate reads it as 'stretched too far'.
The heat rule (src/sim/electrical.ts:49) is linear in overload, `(amps/rating−1)·dt`, and kills a cable at heat 2. So 4 on 3 (133%) is dead in 6 s (log: dead between +4.5 and +6.3 s). Joule heating goes as I²R, and a cable 33% over warms over minutes. The 6 s is acceptable as tuning, but it is not labelled as tuning (DR-36), and it teaches 'a little over = instant smoke'.
findings.fix:
Show heat with a different language: an emissive pulsing core plus heat-shimmer sprites and smoke wisps rising from the cable (reuse this.puff along the cable when heat>.4), with the hose tint going toward a dull brown-red 'cooked' rather than the bright strain orange.
Change electrical.ts:49 to `((amps/rating)**2-1)*dt`, which is still about 6 s at 1.33×. Add a comment: '// I²R heating; time scale is tuning, real cables take minutes'.
findings.verify: Retake shot 12: the heated cable is clearly different from a strained one (compare with a held-cable strain crop). Unit test: heat rate at 1.33× equals 0.78/s.
findings.verify_reason: The heat tints WARM #ffa04a and HOT #ff5a3a (lunch-runtime.ts:10,318) nearly match the strain ramp's #ff922f and #f34e56 (src/sim/cable.ts:83). Shot 12 shows the slack thin cable in bright strain-like orange-red. Harness: 4 bars on a 3-bar cable dies at 6.02 s under the linear rule (electrical.ts:49), and there is no tuning comment.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-teach/circuit-check.mjs: '4 on 3 cable dead at 6.02 s (proposed I^2 rule rate 0.778 /s -> 2.57 s)'
findings.fix_correction: The proposed formula is wrong. ((amps/rating)**2-1)*dt gives 0.778/s at 1.33×, so the cable dies in about 2.6 s, not 'still about 6 s'. The finding's own verify line (0.78/s) contradicts its fix line. To keep about 6 s, scale it: edge.heat += ((amps/rating)**2-1)*dt*0.43. Or keep the unscaled I² rate and raise the death threshold from heat>=2 to heat>=4.7 (and the tint thresholds .4/1.2 to match). The unit test should then assert about 0.33/s at 1.33×.

findings.title: The kitchen lamp's cord looks exactly like a thin job cable, is permanently plugged into the feed post, and stretches infinitely
findings.problem:
this.cord is a TubeGeometry from the post (-4,.4,-3.15) to wherever the portable lamp is, recomputed every frame with no length limit (src/lunch-runtime.ts:301-302). It uses colour '#ecE8dc' (:130), the same colour as the thin cables (:139). In shots 04, 06 and 10 a long cream 'thin cable' already runs out of the kitchen post across the kitchen to the lamp by the conveyor.
This causes three problems:
- It suggests the post is already fed, or that a thin cable is sitting there to pick up (a false affordance, DR-17).
- It hides the post's real output wiring.
- Carrying the lamp anywhere (the doc's alternate 'carry the kitchen lamp into the storeroom', docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:44) drags an unlimited cord, which contradicts the room's own finite-cable rule.
findings.fix: Draw the lamp cord in the post's conduit grey (#7d8697), half the thickness, with a small fixed plug moulded into the post. Cap its length at about 6 m: if the lamp is carried beyond that, the cord pulls tight and the lamp drops, or the cord unplugs and the lamp goes dark. Alternatively make the lamp a normal cable load with its own socket.
findings.verify: Retake shot 04: the cord reads as part of the fixture, not a job cable. Carry the lamp 10 m: it does not stretch indefinitely.
findings.verify_reason: The cord is rebuilt every frame from the post to the lamp with no length cap (lunch-runtime.ts:301-302). Shot 04 shows a long cream line from the post across the kitchen. 'Looks exactly like a thin job cable' is overstated. The cord's radius is .025 against the thin hose's .075 (:302 vs :319), and its colour #ecE8dc matches the thin cable's plugs (:139), not the hose tint #ffe2a8 (:10). It still reads as a loose cable out of the post. Unlimited stretch is real and breaks the finite-cable rule.

findings.title: 'Splitters add up' is a listed insight, but splitters are never needed; the summing happens only inside the hard-wired post
findings.problem: The doc lists 'Splitters add up: feeding oven + lamps through one thin cable scorches it' (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:28). In the build, the summing is done by three invisible fixed branches inside the kitchen post (src/lunch-runtime.ts:46), drawn only as floor conduits (shot 05). The three yellow splitters on the power-room floor (src/levels/lunch.ts:10) appear in no spec or intended route (tests/lunch.spec.ts). A player never sees loads join at a splitter and the sum flow back up one cable. The post's internal sum is real but is not something the player builds (DR-26: the concept should be an act).
findings.fix: Either (a) replace the hard-wired post with a splitter the player places at the kitchen (oven, lamp and storeroom-lamp leads end in loose plugs by the post), so that building oven + lamps on one feed is the act that teaches summing; or (b) keep the post but give it a visible three-way manifold with its own pip strip showing 3+½+½=4. Then add one optional splitter puzzle, e.g. the fridge and conveyor sharing cart A through a splitter before the lift.
findings.verify: Spec: a route that uses a splitter to feed two loads and shows the splitter's input cable at the sum. A screenshot of the post or splitter pip strip reading 4.
findings.verify_reason: The post's three fixed branches (lunch-runtime.ts:46) do the summing. A grep of tests/*.ts and tools/debug/*.mjs finds no splitter use in any spec or bench script, and tests/lunch.spec.ts routes the thick cable straight to the post. LEVEL_02:28 still lists 'Splitters add up' as an insight.
extra_evidence: grep 'splitter' tests/ tools/debug/ returns no hits

findings.title: Doc wording still says the capacitor 'absorbs' or 'eats' the kick, and LEVEL_02 describes behaviour the build no longer has
findings.problem:
These lines are still wrong:
- GAME_DESIGN.md:23: 'capacitor carts (absorb a kick only if placed at the load end)'.
- LEVEL_02:38: 'because the capacitor eats the lift's kick'.
- LEVEL_02:17: the capacitor 'only helps the cable between it and the load if it sits at the load end'. In the build it docks within 2 m or does nothing, and it reduces draw on every lead along the route (src/sim/electrical.ts:40-44).
- LEVEL_02:36: the intended solution unplugs the fridge during the bake, but tests/lunch.spec.ts keeps it on.
- LEVEL_02:19: 'Cable in water = short'.
LR11 is therefore still OPEN. The docs are what future content and copy are written from, so the wrong verbs will leak into the game (DR-34).
findings.fix: GAME_DESIGN.md:23 becomes 'capacitor carts (store charge and supply a start-up kick when wired inline at the load)'. LEVEL_02:38 becomes 'because the capacitor supplies the lift's kick'. Rewrite LEVEL_02:17 to describe the docking or inline wiring, LEVEL_02:36 to match the spec, and LEVEL_02:19 per the water fix.
findings.verify: `grep -rn "absorb\|eats" docs/ src/` returns no capacitor hits.
findings.verify_reason: I checked every cited doc line. GAME_DESIGN.md:23 says 'absorb a kick only if placed at the load end'. LEVEL_02:17 says it 'only helps the cable between it and the load', but electrical.ts:40-44 reduces draw on every lead of the route, source to cap included. LEVEL_02:19 says 'Cable in water = short'. LEVEL_02:36 has the fridge unplugged during the bake, while the spec keeps it on (tests/lunch.spec.ts:19-20). LEVEL_02:38 says 'the capacitor eats the lift's kick'.
extra_evidence: docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:27 (oven+lamps+fridge on B rationale that the spec doesn't follow)

findings.title: The capacitor hint badge is hidden if the lift is tried before the storeroom is lit, and its schematic glyph means nothing to a novice
findings.problem: capBadge.visible requires `this.prop('capacitor').mesh.visible` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:328), and the cart mesh is hidden while the storeroom is dark (:293). A player who explores and tries the lift first (as in my kick run) trips cart A, capHint becomes true, and no badge appears anywhere (shot 23 survey). The marker is on another step, so nothing is pointed at either. Separately, the badge glyph (:57-58) is two plates between lines, the schematic capacitor symbol, which a player learning electronics through play has never been shown.
findings.fix: When the hint is latched but the cart is hidden in the dark, show the badge over the storeroom door (-7.8,-1.8) or the storeroom lamp instead. Use the cart's own look as the glyph (four blue cans with a lightning bolt), and optionally show the schematic symbol beneath it once the player has docked it, so the symbol gets learned.
findings.verify: Rerun s2-fails.mjs kick and take a survey: a badge is visible at the storeroom entrance. Retake after docking: the badge is gone.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it (v1.mjs kick, survey shot). With capHint=true and lit=false, the only badge on the map is the trip badge over cart A, and no cap badge appears, because capBadge requires the cart mesh to be visible (lunch-runtime.ts:328, hidden at :293). There is more: the step-6 marker uses prop(g,'capacitor') (objectives.ts:14,49), which returns undefined when the mesh is hidden. So once step 6 is current and the storeroom is dark (for example after the kitchen feed is pulled to free a cart), the marker vanishes too.
extra_evidence: src/ui/objectives.ts:14 (prop() returns undefined for invisible meshes)

findings.title: Unit and naming gaps: the fridge bonus is '80%' of a unitless thermometer, 'bars' is never defined, and carts 'A' and 'B' carry no letters
findings.problem: The bonus 'Keep the fridge from spoiling (under 80%)' (src/ui/objectives.ts:54) uses a percentage of a thermometer that has no scale (src/lunch-runtime.ts:81, shot 41). Temperatures are not percentages. Prompts say 'cart A' and 'cart B' (src/lunch-runtime.ts:175,189), but the carts show only colours and a bolt (shots 03 and 18). The HUD dials are bare too (shot 17b). 'Bars' appear only in the tagline (src/levels/lunch.ts:15). Each of these is small, but together they make the room's quantities feel arbitrary.
findings.fix: Give the fridge thermometer a simple °C scale (2 °C at the bottom, a 'spoils' band above about 8 °C) and change the bonus to 'Keep the fridge below 8 °C'. Map temperature 0..1 to 2..10 °C in render and in objectives.ts:54. Paint 'A' and 'B' plates on the carts and on the HUD dial bezels. Tie bars to a unit on the cart plaque (see the load-tag finding).
findings.verify: Retake shots 03, 17b and 41: letters and the °C scale are legible at the game camera.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at each cited place. The bonus at objectives.ts:54 reads 'under 80%'. The fridge thermometer (lunch-runtime.ts:81) has no scale. Prompts name 'cart A' and 'cart B' (:175), but in shot 03 the carts show only a bolt decal. The HUD bezels are coloured and carry no letters (lunch-hud.ts:9, shot 17b).

findings.title: The success moment never shows why it worked: no cap discharge in the win shot, Pip out of frame, no recap on the result card
findings.problem: The win push-in frames the lift top and confetti (shot S-38). Pip and the cap cart are cut off at the bottom of the frame, and the cart is not doing anything visible anyway. The result card (shot S-39) shows time, damage, cost and three bonus lines, with nothing that closes the loop on the lesson, e.g. 'the lift wanted 9, cart A only ever saw 4.5'. The player's last memory is of confetti, not of the capacitor carrying the start. DR-28 and Juul's point is that understanding consolidates at the outcome; DR-11 also asks for Pip and the machine in frame.
findings.fix: Frame the win between the winch and the cap cart: winFocus for lunch at about (12,1.2,-5.5), backed off far enough to include Pip at the switch. On the result card for Lunch, add a pictogram strip with no sentence: the lift icon with a '9' spike, a blue cap icon taking the spike, and the cart A dial reading 4.5. Use the recorded peak and draw from the telltale fix.
findings.verify: Retake S-38 and S-39: Pip, the winch and the cap cart are all inside the centre 70% of the frame, and the recap strip numbers match `snapshot().lunch` peak values.
findings.verify_reason: winFocus for lunch is fixed at (12,2.2,-7) (src/game.ts:398). Shot S-38 frames the lift platform and confetti, with Pip and the cap cart cut off at the bottom-left edge. The result card (S-39) shows time, damage, cost and three bonus lines, with no recap of the cap or surge.

findings.title: Every experiment at the lift costs a 25 m round trip to reset cart A, which discourages the try-and-observe loop the room relies on
findings.problem: A trip at the lift (12,-4.8) can only be reset at cart A (-13,3) within 2 m (src/lunch-runtime.ts:162-163). In my kick and trap runs, that is a walk through the corridor and past the bots' line of roughly 25 m each way, about 12–15 s of dead time per experiment (DR-09, DR-20). Walking to the panel is truthful, but the room asks players to experiment (start order, cap or no cap), and each experiment is taxed heavily. The resets also restart every enabled motor at once, so the same trip repeats until the player walks back to the lift and switches something off (shot 26).
findings.fix: Put a remote reset pull-station for each cart on the lift-room wall and the kitchen wall, wired visibly with conduit back to the carts (a real practice: remote trip and reset stations). Or let the cut-out auto-reset after 3 s with all loads switched off, as power stations do, and make the player switch the motors back on one at a time. That second option turns the reset into the stagger lesson itself.
findings.verify: Time from trip to the next attempt in s5-solve trap: under 5 s. A spec asserts that after the auto-reset all motor loads are disabled.
findings.verify_reason: A reset requires standing within 2 m of the cart (lunch-runtime.ts:162-163). Cart A is at (-13,3) and the lift switch at (12,-4.8), about 26 m apart in a straight line and more along the corridor route. Load.enabled survives a trip, so after a reset every enabled motor restarts in the same tick and the cart trips again. The harness's re-trip logic and shot T-38 agree.
extra_evidence: src/sim/electrical.ts:35-39 (enabled loads restart and re-kick after the reset)

notes.teaching:
Lunch Rush has the strongest teaching backbone in the game, and most of its electricity is right at the level taught. Loads on one supply add up against a limit. An undersized cable cooks even when its supply's protection doesn't trip, which is true and a great lesson (E-7). A motor needs a short start-up surge above its running draw. Stored charge at the load supplies that surge, so the supply and cable only see the steady draw. Motors that start together add their surges, so you start them one at a time. Thermal mass lets a fridge ride through an outage. The capacitor is mandatory: the 9-bar kick is over any cart's 5 whichever cable you use, and the thick cable can't help because the limit is the cart's. So the surge is genuinely the mechanic that decides success.

The problem is that almost none of this can be seen. Loads, budgets and ratings appear nowhere in the world (finding 1). The capacitor never shows charge or discharge (finding 2). Kicks happen in one tick, the needle shows full scale on a dead circuit, and nothing happens at the motor (finding 3). Pulses don't scale with current (finding 9). Four faults share one icon, and there is no cause line (finding 8).

The result is that the room is solved by trial and error plus badge and prompt following. The player learns 'blue cart goes by the lift', not 'stored charge carries the surge'. Truth bugs that would mislead a learner:
- Breakers that trip instantly at 1.2–1.8×. Real B-curve MCBs don't trip at all in 1 s at those levels. Reframing the carts as battery power carts with an overload cut-out makes the whole room truthful at no puzzle cost.
- Any intact cable in water counts as a 'short'.
- The capacitor starts full and charges for free.
- Linear, 6-second cable cooking.
- The doc verbs 'absorb' and 'eats'.
There is one real moment of applying the idea: once you know the lift kicks, choosing thin versus thick for the kitchen and the start order of the motors. It needs the surge made visible before it can count as applied understanding.
notes.clarity:
The card and prompt are the only words allowed, and in the two most instructive failures they actively mislead. The 'feed post' and 'leak' steps tick done when a scorching or shorting cable is merely plugged in, and the card then says 'Keep the oven on' while the oven is dead (shots 13, 16). The lift step ticks even when the breaker trips seconds later (trap run, T-37). The fridge, which can fail the job at 120 s, is never a step.

Other naming problems: 'Repair the burned cable' is shown for a door-cut cable. The carts are named A and B in prompts but carry no letters. The fridge bonus is '80%' of a unitless thermometer. 'Bars' are undefined. The kitchen-lamp cord is the same cream colour as a thin cable and stretches infinitely out of the post.

What reads well:
- The HUD chain (oven → belt → lift with progress rings) and the thermometer.
- The cart-coloured dial bezels.
- Socket rings that pulse while you hold a plug.
- The orange then black cable when overheated.
- The puddle badge placed at the leak.
- The sad-food icon and puffs before a spoil.
- Icon-only fail cards that are clear and retry instantly (R).
notes.fun: The physical comedy is intact: door pinches, bots dragging plugs, the dolly-hauled thick cable, smoke from the oven, groaning crowds. The full solve is a satisfying chain, about 95 s scripted and 3–6 min for a human. The best fun beat, though (the lift lurching up on borrowed charge), is invisible, and the win shot frames confetti on a lift top without Pip or the cap cart. Experiments are taxed by 25 m walks to reset cart A, and a reset restarts every enabled motor, so the same trip repeats. That makes failing feel like a chore rather than a joke. Seeing the surge (telltale needle, winch jerk, cap cans dumping) would make the failures and the success both funnier and more instructive.
notes.playability:
Every scripted state was reachable through the capture helper: start, survey, thin-cable scorch, water short with a re-trip on reset while wet, lift kick trip, the intended solve to the A result card, the lift-then-conveyor trap, spoil at exactly 120 s, and burn at 90 s after baking. Close() returned no console or page errors on any run. Retry from the fail card is instant. Side notes for other reviewers:
- snap().drawCalls read 1243 at the start with fullfx (LR15 claimed about 175; possible regression, perf reviewer to confirm).
- My scripted walks stalled at the closed door and at the lift divider (expected).
- Pressing E near the wedged door picks the wedge back up, which re-closes the door (DR-18).
notes.models: Not my dimension. The capacitor cart's four blue cans read well as electrolytic capacitors, and the supply carts read as power carts. Neither model carries state: the cap LED is static, and the carts have no letters and no budget pips. Those additions are specified in findings 1 and 2.

rechecked: LR4 (in-world fail beat before the card): FIXED. Sad icon, puffs and groan show about 1.2 s before the spoil card (shots 42, 43); the burn shows the hot window and smoke from 60 s (shot 45).

LR8 (card prints methods): STILL OPEN. 'with the doorstop', '(or bridge it)' and '(oven and lamps)' remain (src/ui/objectives.ts:42-44). Worse, steps 2 and 3 now latch on a failing plug-in (finding 6).

LR9 (capacitor inline, docks): FIXED in logic. The lift route must pass through the 'cap' node and the cap cord draws while docked (shot S-33). Readability is weak: the cord is a thin dark tube, and nothing shows the cap acting (finding 2).
LR10 (no recharge while tripped): FIXED. electrical.ts:34 requires routes.has(cap.node) and tripped sources build no routes. Charging is still free of current (E-2, finding 2).
LR12 (bars never map to a unit): STILL OPEN (finding 1, finding 16).

LR13 (invisible hard-wired post): PARTIAL. Floor conduits to the oven and storeroom lamp are drawn (shot 05), but the cream kitchen-lamp cord looks like a job cable (finding 12) and the post's summing is not readable (finding 13).
DR-33 water rule (Known): STILL OPEN. An intact thick cable through the leak shorts cart B (shot 16).
DR-29 idle flowing dots: not present in Lunch (the hint is disabled when g.lunch). Lunch pulses appear only on live cables. OK.
LR15 draw calls: possible REGRESSION. snap().drawCalls = 1243 at start with fullfx (PROGRESS claims about 175); not my dimension, flag for the perf reviewer.

DR-07 Lunch time grade: the scripted clean run finished at 1:35, which is A on time against the 120 s default. A human run will likely be B or C on time while damage gives A, so the overall grade stays A.
